data_series.note: Finance data engines (gateway dbnomics, fred). obs_max = observations returned per read (the last ones before T; 240 = 20 years monthly, a reading budget, not a measured optimum). dbnomics_datasets = datasets of the DBnomics search whose matching series are listed (one request each, 2 s pacing). dbnomics_candidates = datasets read from the one /search request and re-ranked locally (DBnomics orders them by number of matching series, not by relevance: live check of 2026-10-29, 'euro area inflation' put ECB CSEC first, 23,959 matching series, no query word in its name). dbnomics_series_pool = series read per opened dataset and re-ranked by the query words in their names (DBnomics returns them in code order). Reading bounds, not measured optima.

oversample.note: search-openalex asks OpenAlex for n works per page, then the local barrier (publication date, forbidden DOIs and titles, Crossref deposit recheck) removes some of them: openalex_extra_pages = most pages requested beyond the first (one OpenAlex request and one Crossref batch each) until n works pass or OpenAlex is exhausted; 0 = the v0.6.0 single page. A bound on requests, not a measured optimum (live check of 2026-10-29, 'graph neural network', T 2020-01-01, n 20: 7 works passed on one page, 20 after 3 pages).

software_heritage.note: provenance <origin>: the last visit with a snapshot dated before T is searched in the origin's visit list (newest first, visits_per_page per request = the API maximum, checked live on 2026-10-29), by bisection on the visit number; visit_requests = most visit-list requests per origin (8 x 100 covers up to ~25,000 visits by bisection). Not found within the bound or no visit before T -> refusal 'unavailable before T', never the latest visit.

linked_sources.note: Sources wired in v0.5.7 (tools/sources/unpaywall.py, opencitations.py, edgar.py, ghsa.py, datacite.py). unpaywall_dois = most DOIs looked up by one search-unpaywall call (one request each). opencitations_complement = citing/references of a DOI add the OpenCitations works not already listed (after the existing ones, within n); false = the v0.5.6 output exactly. opencitations_max = most OpenCitations works per DOI and direction kept after the date filter and rechecked on Crossref (batches of 40; one OpenCitations request per direction reads every row). sec_interval = seconds between two calls to one SEC host (SEC fair access: at most 10 requests/s per user, all machines; 0.5 s = 2/s, under the 4/s of the lab prototype that saw no 429). sec_submission_files = older submissions files (beyond the recent 1,000 filings) scanned by read edgar:. sec_text_chars = characters of the filing's primary document served by read (start of the text). ghsa_types = GitHub advisory type listed by the advisories command (reviewed: curated by GitHub; unreviewed: raw NVD imports). Bounds of politeness and reading, not measured optima.

note: call_cap.default = safety cap on gateway calls when no plugin and no --cap gives one (measured on our benches: 60 calls). review_title_threshold = token overlap above which a title is treated as a forbidden review. code_intervals = minimum seconds between two calls to the same host for the code engines; <host>+token = the interval when a credential is sent (Software Heritage: 120 req/h documented and about 10/min observed anonymous -> 6 s; 1,200 req/h with SWH_TOKEN -> 3 s).

verifier.note: One call per card; above max_chars_per_call (characters of sources), one call per source. A threshold to measure, not a fixed reference value. model: per host profile, '' = the search model (VP_SEARCH_MODEL, else search_model) for the claude profile and the host CLI's own default for openai (no model name fixed here; VP_MODEL or --model override it; the lab measure of 2026-10-26 used claude-opus-5-5, and the 2026-10-28 duel ran it on the 'opus' alias that was the default then). call_cap = gateway calls of the verifier, its own pool (gateway counter-<run>.verifier.txt), outside the searches' cap: in the duel of 2026-10-28 the shared cap of 60 was reached in 7 of 9 runs and up to 54/54 claims ended SOURCE-UNAVAILABLE; the verifier reads at most one record per cited source, and the 10 cards of that duel cited 11 to 39 sources (median 17.5): 60 (the lab's search cap) covers the largest card measured with a 1.5x margin while still bounding a runaway card. fulltext = with --T, fetch the pinned full text (last version before T, verifier/fetch_fulltext.py) of the sources carrying the most claims, no gateway call; false = abstracts only (--fulltext / --no-fulltext override it). sandbox_failure_markers = lower-case markers of a Codex sandbox that cannot start, looked for in the output of the failed shell commands of a `codex exec --json` stream (live check of 2026-10-29 in a container without unprivileged user namespaces: 'bwrap: No permissions to create a new namespace...'); when every shell command of a call failed and one carries a marker, the verifier stops calling the model, writes host_problem in its output and receipt, and exits 3 (claims UNVERIFIED with the reason, never silently). fulltext_cap = full-text attempts per verification (a failure counts): the value frozen for the duel of 2026-10-28 and exercised there (12 of 12 texts obtained in AN13, 4 of 4 in AN01, no reading after T; verifier cost 3.10 USD on 12 texts, the highest measured), not an optimum.

windows.note: Claim windows (tools/verifier/windows.py): mode 'windows' sends the model, for a source longer than head_chars + windows_per_claim x window_chars, only the windows chosen by code for its claims (exact substrings of the retrieved text: for each figure of the claim found in the text the best window holding it, then BM25, plus the head of the text); 'whole' = every source whole, the behaviour of v0.5.1 (checked identical on the 10 cards of the 2026-10-28 duel with a fake engine), also --windows whole. Values chosen offline (no model) on the sources the v0.5.1 verifier actually read in the 5 M runs of that duel (78 sources, 1.82 M characters, 245 FOUND/DISTORTED claims with 424 machine-checked fragments), grid window_chars 600-3000 x windows_per_claim 2-6 x head_chars 0-3000 x number_weight 1-3: 1000 x 6 + head 1500 sends 20 % of the characters before any re-reading, keeps 97.4 % of the cited fragments and at least one cited fragment for 245/245 claims (1500 x 4: same volume, 244/245; 600 x 6: 16 %, 244/245); window_chars >= 600 so that the half-window stride holds any 300-character fragment (ROLE.md bound) whole. number_weight = weight of a figure in the BM25 query: no measurable effect between 1 and 3 (the figure guarantee does the work), 2 kept. escalate_statuses = verdicts given on windows that are judged again on the whole text of their source in a second call (ABSENT and SOURCE-UNAVAILABLE: the only verdicts a missing window can manufacture; DISTORTED needs a machine-checked fragment showing the right value); escalation_max_chars = longest source re-read whole: 200,000 = max_chars_per_call, above every source measured (largest 159,849); above it the claim is UNVERIFIED with the reason, never ABSENT. Replaying the duel's own verdicts offline, windows + re-reading send 64 % of the characters of the whole mode and 18 model calls instead of 55 (T-LAW M 16 -> 2, RAG M 14 -> 4, AN13 M 18 -> 4). Not yet measured with a model: see the verifier bench before treating these values as optima.

claude.note: Claude Code host: the prompt goes on stdin; the caller adds --allowedTools / --disallowedTools; cwd = work dir; env without ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN. budget_args = added by tools/verifier.py under a spending limit (a user budget, state/budget.json), '{usd}' = what the call may still spend; the openai profile has none (stopped between calls only).

openai.note: Codex CLI host: the prompt goes on stdin ('-'), read-only sandbox, web search disabled; cwd = work dir.

general.note: General mode of tools/contradictor.py (any plugin but code): sources_cap_chars = cap on the source texts sent (sources/<key>/source.txt, whole, in key order; a source that does not fit is left out and declared); min_fragment_chars = shortest fragment accepted as verbatim evidence; whole_source_below_chars / window_chars = extract sent to a reread (the whole source when shorter, else this many characters around the fragment); section_chars = cap per report section in the match call; bias_heading = the plugin section joined to the material.

offer.note: Offer of the contradictor after delivery (tools/finish_run.py): when no family is configured (families above, VP_CONTRADICTORS, ~/.config/vp/contradictors), the host profile is not this family, its CLI is found (VP_MODEL_COMMAND_<FAMILY>, else model_command[family].command[0]) and the run has no contradictor.json, one information line in the report's language (tools/report_lang.py, contra_offer) is added to SUMMARY.md and printed last; the user may then ask "contradict this report" (SKILL.md, Contradictor). enabled = false turns the line off. minutes = the time the contradictor added on our benches on 2 reports of 2026-10-29 (general mode, Codex then the match call, rereads and the application: about 2 min in a first trial, 3.5 to 4 min in a second), a range shown to the user, not a bound.

contradictor.note: Optional contradictor after the report (tools/contradictor.py): code plugin = the whole-reading material, any other plugin = general mode after the verification (block general). families: empty = option absent; set it here, or VP_CONTRADICTORS, or ~/.config/vp/contradictors. A family is <via>[:<model>]: openai[:<model>] = the Codex CLI (openai host profile), claude[:<model>] = claude -p (claude host profile), <provider>:<model> = an OpenAI-compatible chat-completions API named in providers (url, key = name of the key variable resolved as in KEYS.md or null for no key, extra = fields merged into the request body, keys_url = where to obtain the key, check_url = a free GET that answers 401/403 to a wrong key, default <url without /chat/completions>/models; both read by tools/setup_keys.py only); add your own provider here or in VP_CONTRADICTOR_PROVIDERS (JSON). No model name is fixed in the code or here: the model id is given in the family (required for an API; for a CLI, empty = the CLI's own default model, so the choice follows the vendor); the models measured on 2026-10-27 are recorded in CHANGELOG.md and plugins/code.md. request = body fields of the measure (temperature 0, 8,000 output tokens). y_cap_chars = the cut of Y used in the measure. max_usd = ceiling on the match call and the rereads (host model) per run, checked before each call with reread_usd_per_call as the estimate; a CLI on a subscription (openai profile) reports 0, so the ceiling only bites on metered hosts; reread_model per host profile: empty = the host CLI's default model (--model / VP_MODEL override it).

cs_engines.note: Gentleness bounds of the CS engines (gateway.py, v0.4.6), not reference values: pmlr_volumes = number of PMLR venues (gateway.PMLR_VENUES, in priority order) whose newest volume published before T is searched (one RSS feed of 1-3 MB each, cached); cvf_conferences = newest CVF main conferences published before T searched (one listing of 3-12 MB each, cached); w3c_lookups = W3C title hits dated per search (one call each); hf_commit_pages = pages of 100 commits walked to find the last commit before T (else the card is refused).

text_terms.note: Content terms of tools/evidence_bank.py and tools/contradictions.py: a word of at least min_term_chars letters, lower-cased, light plural stemming, not in stopwords (English function words plus the reporting words every report sentence uses, which would tie any sentence to any quote). A reading convention, not a measured value.

evidence_bank.note: Optional quote-first writing mode (tools/evidence_bank.py, SKILL.md 'Quote-first writing'). min_shared_terms = content terms a report sentence must share with the quotes of its cited sources to count as supported (with every figure): 1 is the topic word alone, which any sentence on the subject shares, so 2 is the smallest value that ties a statement to a quote; not measured. ignore_years = years (1800-2100, no decimals) are not required in the quote, since the year comes from the record, not the passage. max_quote_chars = longest quote accepted: four times the 300-character verifier fragment bound of ROLE.md, so a whole paragraph-length sentence group fits. shown_chars = display cut in EVIDENCE.md / EVIDENCE.html. cache_max_bytes = gateway answers larger than this are not searched (binary files and full PDFs). skip_sections = report sections not tied (the bibliography and the appendix carry no claim of fact). record_id_max_chars = EB5 attribution inside a cache answer: a JSON object or XML element is the record of an identifier when one of its own fields of at most this many characters names it (identifier, URL or short label fields; long text fields such as an abstract that merely mention another identifier do not make a record); the same order of size as the 300-character verifier fragment bound, not measured.

contradictions.note: Optional contradiction hunt (tools/contradictions.py, SKILL.md 'Contradiction hunt'): mechanical detection only, shown to the reader, never used to filter or correct a claim; the judgment is the model's (verdicts = the labels it may give, written in contradictions-judged.json). statuses = verdict statuses whose claims are compared (ABSENT and INVALID claims leave the run in section 7). min_shared_terms = content terms two passages must share to be on the same topic, unless they share a named entity or are co-cited in one report sentence (then 1): same reading as evidence_bank.min_shared_terms. window_words = words on each side of a marker read as its context (about half a clause); number_window_words = words before a figure read as the name of its measure (plus its unit and the word after: 'sensitivity of 62.8 %'); label_words = words after which a figure is a label, not a measure ('Article 16', 'Table 2', 'C-131/12'). number_rel_tol = relative gap under which two figures on the same measure are taken as equal, on top of their rounding (half a unit of the least precise figure); 0 = rounding only. max_candidates / max_per_source_pair = display bounds so one pair of long sources cannot fill the list. Lexicons: English words of direction, of negative polarity and of decisions (law); a plugin may need more, add them here. None of these values is measured.

passages.note: Cited passages (tools/passages.py, shown by export_report.py under each bibliography entry and written by export_data.py to PASSAGES.md / passages.json). max_chars = longest passage shown per fragment: 300 is the upper bound ROLE.md already sets on a verifier fragment, so a passage is widened to its whole sentence only when that sentence is no longer than what the verifier itself may quote (about 45-50 words, roughly ten seconds of reading); a longer fragment is cut at a word boundary and flagged. max_per_claim = passages shown per claim: 4 is the ROLE.md upper bound on fragments per verdict, so no machine-checked fragment is dropped. Both are reading bounds taken from the role contract, not measured optima.

prisma.note: Optional PRISMA 2020 flow diagram (tools/prisma.py; finish_run.py --prisma, export_report.py --prisma). reasons_max = exclusion reasons listed in the 'Reports excluded' box, the rest summed as 'other recorded reasons'; reason_chars = longest reason shown (cut at a word); mark_window = characters around an 'excluded' mark searched for words saying it is not a screening decision (post-T, gateway, '-leaning'...). svg = layout of the plain SVG (pixels; chars_per_line = wrap width of the main boxes). Display bounds, not measured values.

followups.note: Optional follow-up questions (tools/followups.py; finish_run.py --followups, export_report.py --followups). min/max = questions sought (3 to 5, the user's request of 2026-10-28); fewer derivable = fewer written, never invented. claim_chars / why_chars / angle_chars = longest quotation of a claim, of a verifier discrepancy and of a scope angle inside a question (cut at a word). templates (optional object) overrides the fixed English templates by name (distorted, absent, unavailable_claim, unavailable_source, unread, angle, empty, conflict, contradictor). Display bounds, not measured values.

prior_art.note: Optional 'Prior art?' mode (tools/prior_art.py; validate_card.py --prior-art; finish_run.py --prior-art). elements_max = most elements an idea is cut into (an idea needing more is a project, not a prior-art question); closest = closest sources listed; queries_max = queries listed in 'What was searched' (the rest counted, all in state/journal.jsonl); claim_chars / idea_chars = longest claim, fragment or idea quoted. Not measured: reading bounds of the answer.

runs.run: v0.6.0 ergonomics trials, run A re-measured (cs-ai, no budget)
budget trial of 2026-10-29, R1 (cs-ai, budget 2 USD)
budget trial of 2026-10-29, R2 (biology, budget 2 USD)
duel B6 of 2026-10-29, E1 (biology, local documents)

trace_calibration.note: Full runs with a Sonnet orchestrator and Sonnet searchers, 2026-10-29: calls = search calls of state/journal.jsonl, usd = total_cost_usd of the orchestrator trace (searchers included, verifier excluded). tools/cost.py derives from them trace_usd_per_call = least-squares slope of usd on calls, and trace_usd_fixed = the highest intercept that keeps every run under the line (rounded up to the cent): an upper envelope, not a mean.

costs.note: Estimates shown by tools/cost.py before an expensive mode (SKILL.md section 0 'Cost and budget'); every figure comes from a measure written in CHANGELOG.md / README.md / USAGE.md, none is a price list. standard_usd = academic question, standard mode, Claude Code (Opus orchestrator, Sonnet searchers), verification included: 2.8 to 3.0 USD measured (USAGE section 6; README 'about 2-3 USD'). law_usd = legal texts read whole by the verifier: up to about 10 USD (USAGE section 6; v0.5.1 mechanics duel, T-LAW 10.03 USD). code_whole_reading_usd = code study with the whole reading before verdicts, about 7 USD (README; the whole reading alone 0.9 to 2.6 USD, CHANGELOG v0.1). fulltext_usd_per_text = verifier cost per full text read: about 9 USD-equivalent for the 12 texts of one report (CHANGELOG v0.5.1, USAGE section 6), times verifier.fulltext_cap (the high end); fulltext_extra_low_usd = the smallest extra measured with full text on in the v0.5.1 mechanics duel (arm M minus arm C0: D05 and D06 1.83 USD; AN13 9.35, T-LAW 6.52, RAG 5.26; couts.json of that duel), the low end. audit_factor = 6 to 7 times the standard mode (CHANGELOG v0.1). contradictor_* = per family: 0.26 USD per API call (OpenRouter, 2026-10-27), 0 for a CLI on a subscription, plus about 0.6 USD of rereads per report (CHANGELOG v0.2.0). Prices change with the models: these are orders of size, not quotes. expensive = the modes announced before launch and switched off by a user budget. budget.waves_full = waves of a full run used to scale the waves under a budget (first wave, one complement, two saturation waves: the smallest run the stopping rule of section 4 allows to end on saturation); budget.min_cap = smallest gateway cap a budget may set (three searchers of five calls: the floor of section 3). Under a user budget the verification is inside the budget: budget.verifier_share of it is reserved for the verifier (a quarter: the reserve SKILL.md already sets for verification in injected-parameters mode), written by cost.py --state to state/budget.json, where tools/verifier.py reads it as its spending limit (it stops calling the model there, claims left UNVERIFIED with the reason); the rest pays the orchestrator and the searchers: gateway cap = (rest - trace_usd_fixed) / trace_usd_per_call (bounded by min_cap and call_cap.default), read from state/budget.json by tools/gateway.py when no --cap is given. trace_usd_per_call and trace_usd_fixed are derived by tools/cost.py from trace_calibration (see its note): a run costs a fixed part (framing, writing, checks, delivery) plus a part per search call; the former single figure, 0.054 USD per call (run A re-measured, 3.21 USD for 60 calls), ignored the fixed part and let a 2 USD budget spend 2.43 USD of trace at 27 calls (0.090 per call, R1 of the 2026-10-29 budget trial). With the four runs of trace_calibration: about 0.038 USD per call plus 1.40 USD fixed, so a budget under about 2.6 USD runs at min_cap and is announced as below the smallest run. Opus orchestrator: 0.085 USD per call at 23 calls, 0.088 at 59 (no fixed part measured), about 1.6 times more than a Sonnet orchestrator. verifier_usd = verifier cost per card on the search model (duel B1 of 2026-10-29, arm S, 5 cards of 17 to 42 claims: 0.17 to 0.31 USD); a reserve below its high end is announced as possibly cutting the verification. Conventions, not measured optima.

summary.note: SUMMARY.md / summary.json (tools/summary.py, run by finish_run.py): the message the assistant copies at the end of a run. answer_sentences / answer_chars = the first sentences of the Executive Summary shown as the answer (citations [n] removed), cut at a word. No confidence level (external audit of 2026-10-29: a level drawn from the FOUND share measures attribution, not coverage nor certainty). Line 'Citations confirmed': the FOUND among all the claims the verifier judged, read on its raw output before the removals of section 7 (state/verifier.json `summary`; never the edited verdicts.json alone), the other statuses and the number removed afterwards. Line 'Coverage': the research angles of scope.md reached by a kept source (a searches/<n>.md naming the angle in its first angle_header_lines lines holds the identifier of a card.json source; not shown when it cannot be counted), the distinct studies of the bibliography (tools/study_family.py), 'fewer than min_sources distinct studies' when it applies (SKILL.md section 5 asks to say so), the finding verdicts. Counts read on the run files, not a calibration: the report's verdicts and the Methodology Appendix remain the reference.

new_run.note: Working directory created by tools/new_run.py when the instruction names none: <prefix>-<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>/ in the current directory, slug = the first slug_words content words of the question (accents removed, ASCII, lower case, hyphens), at most slug_chars characters; never an existing directory (suffix -2, -3...). Stopwords = the frequent words of every language of tools/report_lang.py plus extra_stopwords. Naming conventions.

followup.note: Follow-up in the conversation (SKILL.md 'Follow-up in the conversation', tools/followup.py): a short complementary run in <run>/followups/<n>/ (its own scope.md, searches/, REPORT.md, card.json, result.json, verdicts.json, state/ with the parent's gateway cache linked), delivered as <run>/FOLLOWUP-<n>.md / .html / .pdf by finish_run.py; the parent's files are never written. summary_words / findings / min_searches = the bounds validate_card.py applies to a follow-up (the eight sections stay); call_cap = gateway cap of the follow-up's searches (a third of call_cap.default); the verifier keeps its own pool. Conventions for a short run, not measured.

study_family.note: tools/study_family.py: the bibliography entries of one run that are one study under several forms (preprint and article, versions, registry record and report), grouped mechanically so that check 14 (tools/cross_source.py) and the source count of tools/summary.py count studies, not documents (SKILL.md section 0 'Identity of sources', section 4 'Triangulate'). Links: same normalised identifier; a recorded Crossref-style relation of relation_types (card.json `relation` or `related`); same registration number (registry_patterns, regular expressions, case-insensitive); title word overlap (Jaccard of the words of min_token_chars letters or more, numbers excluded, minus the frequent words of tools/report_lang.py and extra_stopwords; 0 when a title has fewer than title_min_words such words or when a word of distinct_words is in one title only) >= title_min_similarity with the same first author of the bibliography line (read in its first author_words_max words; not_authors are placeholders, not names), or >= title_only_min_similarity when a first author is missing; title links only between entries at most year_gap_max years apart (preprint to article, full report to journal article, follow-up publication). title_link_kinds = the identifier kinds of scholarly records between which a title link is allowed (court decisions, statutes, data series, code and local documents repeat their title words by construction: in the replay, seven Conseil d'Etat decisions and two sites of one local field trial would have been merged). Replay of the 29/10 cards: the pairs found at 0.6 are true (Martineau BMJ 2017 / HTA 2019 at 0.62 to 0.71; Carter 12 / 24 months at 0.67); the false links seen at lower settings (a pilot trial at 0.54 and 0.64, two sites of one local evaluation, BrowseComp / BrowseComp-Plus, two papers on emergent abilities at 0.83 without a first author) are refused by title_min_words, distinct_words and title_only_min_similarity. The thresholds were set on the constructed cases of tests/test_study_family.py and on the replay of the 29/10 cards (skill-vp/essai-auditfix-29-10): conventions, not a measured F1 per pair. enabled = false makes every entry its own study (the former behaviour).

cross_source.note: Check 14 of validate_card.py (tools/cross_source.py): a clause that compares, ranks, counts, excludes or reports a search outcome across sources while citing a single source. enabled = false switches the check off. excerpt_chars = longest excerpt of a flagged sentence printed (a display bound). skip_sections = canonical titles of the sections not read (the bibliography holds no prose). The marker words are in tools/cross_source.py, one entry per language of tools/report_lang.py.

update.label: VanishingPoint
update.note: Automatic update (tools/auto_update.py), run by tools/check_keys.py --announce at the start of a run, at most once per interval_hours (time of the last check in <HOME>/<config_dir>/<state_file>). auto = default when the user has not answered the setup question (python3 -I tools/auto_update.py --setup writes {"auto": true|false} to <HOME>/<config_dir>/<choice_file>, which wins). The latest version is the highest tag matching tag_pattern on the public repository (remote; empty = the `repository` of the manifest), read by `git ls-remote --tags` without any credential; never a branch. Only when it is strictly higher than the manifest's `version`: with auto, `git fetch` of that tag then a fast-forward only (hooks disabled, no script run), refused (one notice line instead) when tracked files are modified, the branch has diverged, the skill directory is not the top of its own git repository, its path holds one of managed_path_markers (a copy managed by Claude Code's plugin system), VP_OFFLINE=1, or the network fails; without auto, the notice line only. notify = false silences the notice line. timeout_s = limit of each git call (seconds). Any failure prints nothing and never changes the exit code of check_keys.py.

progress.note: tools/progress.py --hook, run by Claude Code after each tool call of the orchestrator (PostToolUse hook of the SKILL.md header; never by the model). Measured 29/10 (skill-vp/essai-progress-29-10): Claude Code 2.1.292 folds tool output ("Ran 1 shell command") and shows it only in the detailed transcript (ctrl+o), so a line printed by a tool is not seen unless the model copies it (copied 5 times out of 8 in the two runs of essai-ergo-263); a hook systemMessage is shown by the host itself ("PostToolUse:Bash says: ..."), in the default view and in stream-json (system/informational). Hooks do not run for sub-agent tool calls. hook_tools = the tools whose calls carry a run path; steps = the order in which each step is shown once (searches: again on each new searcher file); log = file under state/.

possibles.note: tools/read_possibles.py (SKILL.md section 4, before the stop). A candidate line of searches/*.md is one carrying an identifier and a verdict matching verdict_regex; its first identifier counts as already read when the line matches read_basis_regex (basis abstract), and any identifier read by the gateway (`read` in state/journal.jsonl) is already read. At most max_records candidates, in order of first appearance; abstracts by batches of pubmed_batch PMIDs (esummary for the date barrier, then efetch XML) and epmc_batch DOIs (Europe PMC core), then openalex_batch DOIs for those Europe PMC does not index (OpenAlex, abstract from its inverted index, OPENALEX_KEY optional); abstracts cut at abstract_chars and titles at title_chars in state/possibles.md. The batch is journaled under journal_pool (seen, never counted against the searches' cap). These are reading bounds, not measured optima.
